verses.text: Early on the first day of the week, while it was still dark, Mary Magdalene went to the tomb. She saw that the stone had been moved away.
She ran to Simon Peter and the other disciple, the one Jesus loved. “They’ve taken the Lord out of the tomb, and we don’t know where they put him!” she told them.
So Peter and the other disciple headed for the tomb.
They ran together, but the other disciple got there first.
He bent down, looked inside, and saw the linen cloths lying there. But he didn’t go in.
Then Simon Peter arrived and went straight into the tomb. He saw the linen cloths lying there,
and the cloth that had covered Jesus’ head. It wasn’t with the other cloths; it was rolled up by itself.
Then the other disciple, who had reached the tomb first, went in too. He saw, and he believed.
They still didn’t understand from Scripture that Jesus had to rise from the dead.
Then the disciples went back to where they were staying.
Mary stayed outside the tomb, crying. As she wept, she bent down and looked inside.
She saw two angels in white sitting where Jesus’ body had been—one at the head, one at the feet.
They asked her, “Woman, why are you crying?” She said, “They’ve taken away my Lord, and I don’t know where they put him.”
After saying this, she turned around and saw Jesus standing there, but she didn’t realize it was him.
Jesus asked her, “Woman, why are you crying? Who are you looking for?” Thinking he was the gardener, she said, “Sir, if you carried him away, tell me where you put him, and I’ll take him.”
Jesus said, “Mary.” She turned toward him and said, “Rabboni!”—which means “Teacher!”
Jesus told her, “Don’t cling to me; I haven’t yet gone up to my Father. Go to my brothers and tell them, ‘I am going up to my Father and your Father, to my God and your God.’”
Mary Magdalene went to the disciples and told them, “I’ve seen the Lord!” She also told them what he had said to her.

That evening, on the first day of the week, the disciples had locked the doors where they were gathered because they feared the authorities. Jesus came and stood among them. “Peace be with you,” he said.
After saying this, he showed them his hands and his side. The disciples were overjoyed when they saw the Lord. 🙌
Jesus said again, “Peace be with you. Just as the Father sent me, I’m sending you.”
Then he breathed on them and said, “Receive the Holy Spirit.
If you forgive the sins of anyone, they are forgiven. If you leave the sins of anyone unforgiven, they remain unforgiven.
Thomas, one of the Twelve, also called Didymus, wasn’t with them when Jesus came.
The other disciples told him, “We’ve seen the Lord!” But he said, “Unless I see the nail marks in his hands, put my finger where the nails were, and put my hand into his side, I won’t believe it.”
Eight days later, the disciples were inside again, and Thomas was with them. The doors were locked, but Jesus came and stood among them. “Peace be with you,” he said.
Then he said to Thomas, “Put your finger here and look at my hands. Reach out your hand and put it into my side. Don’t stay stuck in doubt; believe.”
Thomas answered him, “My Lord and my God!”
Jesus said, “You believe because you’ve seen me. Blessed are those who haven’t seen me and still believe.”
Jesus did many other signs in front of his disciples that aren’t written in this book.
But these have been written so you may believe that Jesus is the Messiah, the Son of God, and so that by believing you may have life in his name.
